name: Deep Q-Network (DQN)
analogy: Think of it as a trader keeping a scrapbook of past situations and what happened after each choice. A neural network studies random pages from the scrapbook to learn what each choice is worth in each situation, and a frozen copy of its older self provides steady targets so it is not chasing itself.

steps.title: Describe the situation as a state
steps.description: Each bar is turned into a row of numbers, the state: recent returns, indicators, volume and the current position. The network reads this row and nothing else.
steps.inExample: The 10:30 MNQ five-minute bar becomes a row of 40 numbers, including the last 6 returns, the relative strength index, volume against its average and the current position.

steps.title: Estimate the worth of each action
steps.description: The network outputs one number for each available action: short, flat or long. Each number is its estimate of the total reward to come if that action is taken now and good choices follow.
steps.inExample: For this state the network outputs about minus 4, plus 1 and plus 8 US dollars for short, flat and long.

steps.title: Mostly pick the best, sometimes explore
steps.description: To collect experience, the agent usually takes the action with the highest estimate but occasionally picks one at random. The chance of a random pick starts very high and is lowered as training goes on.
steps.inExample: At the start about 9 bars in 10 are a random choice. Late in training only 1 bar in 20 is random.

steps.title: Store each experience in a replay buffer
steps.description: After every bar the agent saves what it saw, what it did, the reward and the next state. The store holds a large pool of past experience from all stages of training.
steps.inExample: The buffer holds the most recent 100,000 transitions from the training window.

steps.title: Learn from random batches of the past
steps.description: Instead of learning from the last few bars, the network learns from a random batch drawn from the buffer. Mixing old and new experience stops it from overfitting to whatever just happened and lets it reuse each bar many times.
steps.inExample: Each learning step draws 64 random transitions from different days and months.

steps.title: Aim at a slowly changing target
steps.description: The learning target for each transition is the reward plus the best estimated worth of the next state. That worth comes from a frozen copy of the network, refreshed only every so often, so the targets hold still while the main network learns.
steps.inExample: The frozen copy is updated every 1,000 learning steps, and in between it supplies the targets.

useFor.example: Learning short, flat or long decisions on MNQ five-minute bars from a state of recent features and the current position.

useFor.task: Getting more from a fixed stretch of history
useFor.example: Replaying the same 12 months of bars thousands of times in different random mixes, instead of passing over them once.

useFor.task: A baseline for fancier value-based agents
useFor.example: Establishing the result that Double, Dueling or prioritised variants must beat on the same walk-forward folds.

useFor.task: Seeing what the agent thinks each state is worth
useFor.example: Plotting the three action estimates over a trading day to see where it expects short, flat or long to pay.

avoidWhen: Actions are continuous, such as choosing any position size; a method that outputs a size directly fits better than one that needs a fixed list of choices.
Rewards are extremely noisy; the estimates of worth chase the noise and can be overstated, and a calmer variant or a supervised model is safer.

example.scenario: A trained agent reads the 10:30 five-minute bar on MNQ and must choose between short, flat and long. The agent holds no position.

input.summary: One row of state features describing the bar and the current position.

fields.name: close
fields.meaning: The price at which the 10:30 five-minute bar closed.

fields.name: price change over the last 6 bars
fields.meaning: How much price rose over the previous 30 minutes, about a fifth of a percent.

fields.name: relative strength index, 14 bars
fields.meaning: A momentum reading from 0 to 100; above 50 means recent buying.

fields.name: volume against its 20-bar average
fields.meaning: How heavy trading was compared with the recent norm.

fields.name: average true range, 14 bars
fields.meaning: The typical high-to-low travel of a recent bar.

output.summary: An estimated worth for each action and the action the agent picks.

fields.name: estimated worth of short
fields.meaning: The total reward the network expects if it goes short now.

fields.name: estimated worth of flat
fields.meaning: The total reward expected from standing aside.

fields.name: estimated worth of long
fields.meaning: The total reward expected from going long.

fields.name: action taken
fields.meaning: The action with the highest estimate.

example.reading: Read the gap between the best and second best estimate: a gap of 7 dollars is a clear preference, a gap of under 1 dollar is a coin toss that costs would erase. The estimates are the network's opinion and tend to run optimistic, so judge the agent by results on held-out folds after costs.
